title: Exact functors have vanishing higher right derived functors
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let v:A\to B be an exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For every object M of A, the right derived functors R^qv(M) defined from injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] vanish for all integers q>0.

proof.text: Because v is exact, it is in particular left exact and additive, so the right derived functors in the statement are defined by choosing an injective resolution M -> I^\bullet as in [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The resolution has H^q(I^\bullet)=0 for every q>0.

source.place: Lemma 015F (derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof: choose an injective resolution and use exactness of F

proof.text: Apply the natural cohomology isomorphism for an exact functor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to I^\bullet. For each q>0 it gives H^q(v(I^\bullet)) \cong v(H^q(I^\bullet))=v(0)=0, so H^q(v(I^\bullet)) is zero.

source.place: Lemma 015F (derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof: F transforms quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms because it preserves cohomology

proof.text: By the definition of the right derived functors in [def-sp-left-exact-additive], R^qv(M)=H^q(v(I^\bullet)) for the chosen injective resolution. The vanishing from Step 2 therefore gives R^qv(M)=0 for every integer q>0.
